To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immunohistochemistry of P-gp is sensitive to fixation and staining variables, and that seizures induce overexpression of this protein in four different cell-types, i.e., capillary endothelial cell, perivascular and astroglia, and hippocampal neurons.
P-gp expression is induced in four different cell populations after seizures, but the immunohistochemistry of P-gp is sensitive to fixation and staining variables.

P-gp expression is increased by seizures in four cell types, i. e., EC, per-ivascular astrocy-tes, parench-ymal astro-cytes, and neurons; that the immunolocaliza-tion of P-gp depends on the fixation method and the antibody used; and that, when using paraformaldehyde fixed sections, the immunohistochemi-cal detection of increased P-gp expression in astrocytes and neurons is more sensitive to fixation
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemistry of P-gp, which is an important drug-efflux pump, in normal rat brain as well as after seizures.
the development and application of immunohistochemical methods for the detection of P-gp overexpression in the rat brain.
the question whether the P-gp expression in the brain parenchyma is increased in epilepsy and, if so, in which cells and to what extent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the immunohistochemically detectable P-gp expression in the brain depends on the fixation conditions, and that the increased expression of P-gp after seizures is most likely a consequence of increased expression in EC, perivacular astrocytes, neurons, and, to a much smaller extent, in parenchymal (nonperivascular) astrocytes.
P-gp overexpression is induced in all cell types that contribute to the BBB and in neurons, and that the expression of P-gp is not confined to EC.
the immunohistochemistry of P-gp is a very delicate technique that requires careful attention to fixation and staining variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P-gp is a highly dynamic protein in the brain, which may be involved in various aspects of BBB function and brain pathology.

P-gp immunoreactivity in rat brain depends on fixation conditions and that P-gp overexpression after seizures is detected in all cell types of the BBB, i.e., in EC, astrocytes, perivascular, and parenchymally distributed.
P-gp is expressed by EC of the BBB, parenchyma astrocytes, perivascular (penetrating) astrocytes, but not by neurons, in normal brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of the immunohistochemistry technique and the antibody used to detect P-gp expression should be considered very carefully, as it may lead to conflicting conclusions regarding P-gp expression and localization in the normal and epileptic brain.
immunolabeling of the P-gp protein in brain tissue depends strongly on fixation and staining conditions, which should be carefully considered when comparing different studies.
immunohistochemical studies on the localization of proteins in the central nervous system (CNS) should always be done with a combination of different fixation techniques and antibodies.
